methodological_rigor.justification: Well-designed mechanistic cell-based study using UPS cell line (JBT19) and primary PBMCs to examine IFNγ effects on chemoresistance and immune sensitivity. Multiple assays (flow cytometry, MTT, cell cycle, annexin V, functional killing assays) employed with appropriate controls. Statistics include t-tests, ANOVA with Tukey post hoc, and are generally properly applied. Reversibility experiments strengthen conclusions. Limited to single cell line; no animal models. Controls appropriate (PC-3 as comparison).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: LoE 5 (preclinical cell-based mechanistic work). Investigates dual role of IFNγ in chemoresistance and immunotherapy. Translational implications for combining therapies speculative; no patient samples, in vivo models, or clinical outcomes studied. Direct clinical application path unclear.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods detailed with antibody catalogs, flow cytometry protocols, concentrations, and timing. Cell line authentication mentioned (passages <20 from vendor). Ethical approval documented (EK-602.4/22). However, ARRIVE is not applicable (not animal study); methods are cell-based. Data availability not explicitly stated. Some supplementary details would benefit from tables.

novelty_literature.justification: Dual role of IFNγ (immune stimulation + chemoresistance) in UPS is novel as far as stated ('to the best of our knowledge, present study demonstrated dual role...for the first time'). However, IFNγ upregulation of checkpoint molecules (PD-L1, MHC) and immune evasion mechanisms are known. The specific combination and reversibility in UPS is the novel contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized methods, clear results with logical progression from phenotype to mechanistic validation. Figures are informative with appropriate statistical annotations. Discussion contextualizes findings and acknowledges limitations (single cell line, lack of in vivo validation). Some lengthy sections; generally readable.

key_strengths: Novel dual role of IFNγ in promoting chemoresistance while enhancing immune sensitivity in UPS cells.
Comprehensive phenotypic characterization (CD44, CD47, CD95, MHC-I, MHC-II, PD-L1) across multiple timepoints.
Functional validation: JBT19-reactive lymphocytes effectively kill both IFNγ-treated and untreated cells, overcoming chemoresistance.
Reversibility demonstrated: phenotypic changes and chemoresistance sustained but reversible after 24 days without IFNγ.
key_concerns: Limited to single UPS cell line (JBT19); generalizability to other sarcomas unclear.
No in vivo xenograft or genetically engineered mouse models for validation.
Mechanism of docetaxel resistance not fully elucidated (no MDR-1, Bcl-2, apoptosis involvement detected).
Proposed therapeutic combination (immunotherapy + chemotherapy) remains speculative without patient or animal data.
PBMC donors limited (4 healthy volunteers); patient-derived TILs would strengthen findings.
chief_reviewer.rationale: Rigorous preclinical mechanistic study documenting novel dual role of IFNγ in promoting both chemoresistance and immunostimulation in UPS, with functional validation. Limited to single cell line and lacks in vivo confirmation, but methodology is sound and findings support minor revision for tier 4 publication.
